S1.title: Wikipedia EN, Roman Kingdom
S1.quote: 753 BC, with settlements around the Palatine Hill along the river Tiber in central Italy … a significant number for a population of 3,000 Latins … Among these were Rome's great sewer systems, the Cloaca Maxima, which he used to drain the swamp-like area between the Seven Hills of Rome. … Lucius Tarquinius Priscus was the fifth king of Rome and the first of Etruscan birth.

S2.title: Wikipedia EN, Roman Republic
S2.quote: beginning with the overthrow of the Roman Kingdom (traditionally dated to 509 BC) and ending in 27 BC with the establishment of the Roman Empire … was expelled from Rome in 509 BC

S3.title: Wikipedia EN, Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus
S3.quote: Traditionally dedicated in 509 BC, the first building was the oldest and most important large temple in Archaic Rome.

S4.title: Wikipedia EN, Servian Wall
S4.quote: is dated by Livy to have been completed in 378 BC … enclosed a total area of 246 hectares (610 acres) … The largest section is preserved outside the Termini Station … Expanding domestic structures simply incorporated existing wall sections into their foundations

S5.title: Wikipedia EN, Circus Maximus
S5.quote: Permanent wooden starting stalls were built in 329 BC. … It measured 621 m (2,037 ft) in length and 118 m (387 ft) in width … it was the first and largest stadium in ancient Rome and its later Empire

S6.title: Wikipedia EN, Colosseum
S6.quote: in 72 and was completed in AD 80 under his successor and heir, Titus … Severe damage was inflicted on the Colosseum by the great earthquake in 1349, causing the outer south side, lying on a less stable alluvial terrain, to collapse.

S7.title: Wikipedia EN, Theatre of Marcellus
S7.quote: it was completed in 13 BC and formally inaugurated in 12 BC by Augustus

S8.title: Wikipedia EN, Mausoleum of Augustus
S8.quote: a large tomb built by the Roman emperor Augustus in 28 BC on the Campus Martius … The completed mausoleum measured 90 m (295 ft) in diameter by 42 m (137 ft) in height.

S9.title: Wikipedia EN, Trajan's Column
S9.quote: Completed and dedicated on 12 May 113 AD … The structure is about 30 metres (98 feet) in height, 35 metres (115 feet) including its large pedestal.

S10.title: Wikipedia EN, Pantheon, Rome
S10.quote: originally built under Roman emperor Augustus (27 BC–AD 14) and reconstructed under Hadrian (117–138) … the present building was completed by the emperor Hadrian and probably dedicated c. AD 126

S11.title: Wikipedia EN, Basilica of Maxentius
S11.quote: Construction began on the northern side of the forum under the emperor Maxentius in 308 AD, and was completed in 312 by Constantine I

S12.title: Wikipedia EN, Palatine Hill
S12.quote: Excavations show that people have lived in the area since the 10th century BC. … the ruins of the palaces of at least Augustus (27 BC – 14 AD), Tiberius (14–37 AD) and Domitian (81–96 AD) can still be seen

S13.title: Wikipedia EN, Castel Sant'Angelo
S13.quote: was erected on the right bank (or northern edge) of the Tiber, between 134 and 139 AD … Legend holds that the Archangel Michael appeared atop the mausoleum, sheathing his sword as a sign of the end of the plague of 590

S14.title: Wikipedia EN, Baths of Caracalla
S14.quote: The baths were likely built between AD 212 (or 211) and 216/217 … They were inaugurated in AD 216.

S15.title: Wikipedia EN, Baths of Diocletian
S15.quote: Named after emperor Diocletian and built from AD 298 to 306, they were the largest of the imperial baths.

S16.title: Wikipedia EN, Aurelian Walls
S16.quote: are a line of city walls built between AD 271 and AD 275 in Rome … The full circuit ran for 19 km (12 mi) surrounding an area of 13.7 km2 (5.3 sq mi). … brick-faced concrete, 3.5 m (11 ft) thick and 8 m (26 ft) high, with a square tower every 100 Roman feet (29.6 m (97 ft)) … on the right bank of the Tiber, the Trastevere district … until 20 September 1870, when the Bersaglieri of the Kingdom of Italy breached the wall near the Porta Pia and captured Rome

S17.title: Wikipedia EN, Old St. Peter's Basilica
S17.quote: Construction began by orders of the Roman Emperor Constantine I between 318 and 322 … took about 40 years to complete … in 800, Charlemagne was crowned emperor of the Carolingian Empire there … its last original part being demolished in 1605 … built over the historical site of the Circus of Nero

S18.title: Wikipedia EN, St. Peter's Basilica
S18.quote: Construction of the present basilica began on 18 April 1506 and was completed on 18 November 1626. … Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana brought the dome to completion in 1590, the last year of the reign of Sixtus V. … Peter's rises to a total height of 136.57 metres (448.1 ft)

S19.title: Wikipedia EN, St. Peter's Square
S19.quote: was redesigned by Gian Lorenzo Bernini from 1667 to 1676, under the direction of Pope Alexander VII

S20.title: Wikipedia EN, Leonine City
S20.quote: Built from 848 to 852 as the only extension ever made to the walls of Rome, this three-kilometre wall completely encircled the Vatican Hill for the first time in its history. … The walling was constructed of tuff and tiling, forty feet high, with 44 strong towers at bowshot intervals.

S21.title: Wikipedia EN, Sack of Rome (410)
S21.quote: On 24 August 410 the Visigoths entered Rome through its Salarian Gate, according to some opened by treachery, according to others by want of food, and pillaged the city for three days.

S22.title: Wikipedia EN, Siege of Rome (537-538)
S22.quote: The siege of Rome took place from 2 March 537 to 12 March 538 AD … They proceeded to block the aqueducts that were supplying the city with its water, necessary both for drinking and for operating the gristmills. … First they tried to enter through the Aqua Virgo aqueduct.

S23.title: Wikipedia EN, Gothic War (535-554)
S23.quote: Totila finally entered Rome on 17 December 546, when his men scaled the walls at night and opened the Porta Asinaria.

S24.title: Wikipedia EN, Great Fire of Rome
S24.quote: nearly three quarters of Rome had been destroyed (10 out of 14 districts) … The fire started in the merchant shops around Rome's chariot stadium, Circus Maximus. … in the region of the Circus neighboring the Caelian and Palatine Hills of Rome … began on the evening of 18–19 July 64 AD

S25.title: Wikipedia EN, Sack of Rome (1527)
S25.quote: followed the capture of Rome on 6 May 1527 by the mutinous troops of Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor … Clement VII took refuge in Castel Sant'Angelo

S26.title: Wikipedia EN, Roman Republic (1849)
S26.quote: was a short-lived state declared on 9 February 1849 … The republic was led by Carlo Armellini, Giuseppe Mazzini, and Aurelio Saffi. … The French Army entered Rome on 3 July and reestablished the Holy See's temporal power.

S27.title: Wikipedia EN, Roman Republic (18th century)
S27.quote: was a sister republic of the French First Republic that existed from 1798 to 1799 … It was proclaimed on 15 February 1798 after Louis-Alexandre Berthier, a general of the French Revolutionary Army, had occupied the city of Rome on 11 February. … It proved short-lived, as Neapolitan troops restored the Papal States in October 1799.

S28.title: Wikipedia EN, Capture of Rome
S28.quote: The capture of Rome (Italian: Presa di Roma) occurred on 20 September 1870 … Rome was officially made capital of Italy on 3 February 1871

S29.title: Wikipedia EN, March on Rome
S29.quote: On 28 October, the fascist demonstrators and Blackshirt paramilitaries approached the capital … ascending to power in the Kingdom of Italy

S30.title: Wikipedia EN, Liberation of Rome
S30.quote: The liberation of Rome from German occupation in World War II was carried out on June 3–4, 1944 by American and British troops.

S31.title: Wikipedia EN, Avignon Papacy
S31.quote: Clement refused to move to Rome, and in 1309 he moved his court to the papal enclave at Avignon, where it remained for the next 67 years.

S32.title: Wikipedia EN, Trevi Fountain
S32.quote: completed by Giuseppe Pannini in 1762 … Work began in 1732.

S33.title: Wikipedia EN, 1960 Summer Olympics
S33.quote: were an international multi-sport event held from 25 August to 11 September 1960 in Rome, Italy

S34.title: Wikipedia EN, EUR, Rome
S34.quote: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana (1938–1943) … The area was originally chosen in the 1930s as the site for the 1942 World's Fair which Benito Mussolini planned to open to celebrate twenty years of Fascism

S35.title: Wikipedia EN, Roma Termini railway station
S35.quote: It was inaugurated in 1950. … On 25 February 1863, Pope Pius IX opened the first, temporary Termini Station

S36.title: Wikipedia EN, Vittoriano
S36.quote: a large national monument built between 1885 and 1935 to honour Victor Emmanuel II … The partly completed monument was inaugurated on 4 June 1911

S37.title: Wikipedia EN, Stadio Olimpico (Rome)
S37.quote: it was opened on 17 May 1953 with a football game between Italy and Hungary … The Olimpico hosted the opening and closing ceremonies and track-and-field events of the 1960 Olympics

S38.title: Wikipedia EN, Sack of Rome (1084)
S38.quote: In May 1084, Italo-Normans sacked Rome, the result of the Pope Gregory VII's call for aid from the duke of Apulia, Robert Guiscard.

S39.title: Wikipedia EN, Ostrogothic Kingdom
S39.quote: controlled Italy and neighbouring areas between 493 and 553 … Odoacer had previously become the de facto ruler of Italy

S40.title: Wikipedia EN, Fall of the Western Roman Empire
S40.quote: In 476, the Germanic barbarian king Odoacer deposed the last emperor of the Western Roman Empire in Italy, Romulus Augustulus

S41.title: Wikipedia EN, Papal States
S41.quote: under the direct sovereign rule of the pope from 756 to 1870 … Following the fall of the First French Empire in 1814, the Congress of Vienna (1814–15) formally restored the Italian territories of the Papal States

S42.title: Wikipedia EN, History of Rome
S42.quote: he found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble … Estimates of its peak population range from 450,000 to over 3.5 million people with estimates of 1 to 2 million being most popular with historians. … Rome was annexed by Napoleon and was part of the First French Empire from 1809 to 1814. … Only on 17 January 1377, Gregory XI could finally reinstate the Holy See in Rome. … Rome became the capital of the Italian Republic (established in 1946). … recapturing the city next year, on 9 December AD 536 … the population of Rome fell to as low as 30,000 inhabitants … its population falling below 20,000 … Rome was annexed by Napoleon and was part of the First French Empire from 1809 to 1814.

S43.title: Wikipedia EN, Charlemagne
S43.quote: In 800, Charlemagne was crowned emperor in Rome by Pope Leo III.

S44.title: Wikipedia EN, Battle of the Allia
S44.quote: they decided to send the men of military age, the able-bodied senators and their families to the Capitoline Hill with weapons and provisions to defend the fortress

S45.title: Wikipedia EN, History of Rome (Gallic sack)
S45.quote: The Gauls destroyed much of Rome's historical records when they sacked the city after the Battle of the Allia in 390 BC (according to Polybius, the battle occurred in 387/386)

S46.title: Wikipedia EN, Appian Way
S46.quote: began and completed the first section as a military road to the south in 312 BC

S47.title: Wikipedia EN, Aqua Appia
S47.quote: The Aqua Appia was the first Roman aqueduct, and its construction was begun in 312 BC by the censor Appius Claudius Caecus

S48.title: Wikipedia EN, Third Punic War
S48.quote: In early 146 BC the Romans launched their final assault and, over six days, systematically destroyed the city

S49.title: Wikipedia EN, Assassination of Julius Caesar
S49.quote: Julius Caesar, the Roman dictator, was assassinated on the Ides of March (15 March), 44 BC, by a group of senators

S50.title: Wikipedia EN, Rome
S50.quote: Rome then became the focus of hopes of Italian reunification after the rest of Italy was united as the Kingdom of Italy in 1861 with the temporary capital in Florence. … Rome then became the focus of hopes of Italian reunification … By 550 BC, Rome was the second largest city in Italy after only Taras (modern Taranto) on the Salento Peninsula. It had an area of about 285 ha (700 acres) and an estimated population of 35,000. … After the Gothic Wars, 535–552, the population may have dwindled temporarily to 30,000. … When the Kingdom of Italy annexed Rome in 1870, the city had a population of about 225,000. … He did away with democracy by 1926

S51.title: Wikipedia EN, Lateran Treaty
S51.quote: The Lateran Treaty was one component of the Lateran Pacts of 1929 … The treaty recognised Vatican City as an independent state under the sovereignty of the Holy See.

S52.title: Wikipedia IT, Demografia di Roma
S52.quote: si calcola che Roma possedesse già una popolazione di almeno 30 000 abitanti … con circa 187 000 residenti … Sotto Augusto la popolazione romana si attestava attorno al milione di abitanti … con 1 200 000-1 700 000 residenti stipati in circa 49 000 edifici … fra i 700 000 e il milione di abitanti … ospitava, all'interno delle proprie mura, 650 000 abitanti circa … Il secondo sacco ad opera dei Vandali (455), ben più distruttivo e cruento del precedente … si attestava attorno alle 200 000 unità … non più di 30 000 abitanti alla fine della guerra gotica … gli 80 000 abitanti … 55 035 abitanti … ridottisi però a 20 000 dopo tale luttuoso evento … Nel 1600 Roma aveva raggiunto i 110 000 abitanti … i 156 000 abitanti del 1750

zones.name: First settlements: Palatine, Capitoline and Forum valley
zones.note: Tradition: settlements around the Palatine from 753 BC (S1); people lived there since the 10th century BC (S12). Ring is a HAND SKETCH (+-150 m), not surveyed; born/era_height are hand-set, not data.

zones.name: Servian Rome (walled area, 246 ha)
zones.note: About 285 ha and ~35,000 people by 550 BC (S50); the later wall encloses 246 ha (S4). Ring = legacy outline scaled to 246 ha around its centroid: shape NOT surveyed. born/era_height hand-set.

zones.name: Republican and Imperial Rome within the Aurelian Walls
zones.note: Walls of 271-275 enclose 13.7 km2 (S16); about 49,000 buildings, many multi-storey, at the 2nd-century peak (S52). Born ramp from the Forum outward is a hand-set model, era_height (m) an estimate [Guessing]. The kit has no depopulation: ancient blocks stay until the current building replaces them.

zones.name: Vatican and Leonine City
zones.note: Settlement around Old St. Peter's (begun 318-322) until the Leonine Wall (848-852). Ring is a HAND SKETCH (+-150 m). born/era_height hand-set.

walls.name: Servian Wall
walls.note: Completed 378 BC (Livy, S4); 10 m high, 3.6 m wide, 11 km, 246 ha. Ring: legacy outline scaled to 246 ha, shape not surveyed. Demolition year 271 is a MODELLING CHOICE (Aurelian Walls); the source says only that houses absorbed sections and that the largest section survives at Termini (kept: circle by the station, Wikipedia coordinate).

walls.name: Aurelian Walls
walls.note: Built 271-275; 3.5 m thick, 8 m high, a tower every 29.6 m, 19 km (S16). Heightened to 16 m in the 4th century: not modelled. Outline = legacy ring, checked against 10 gate coordinates (Wikipedia): 15-232 m off the gates; area 1,315 ha vs 1,370 ha documented. Includes Trastevere/Janiculum on the right bank.

walls.name: Leonine Wall
walls.note: Built 848-852, 3 km, forty feet high, 44 towers (S20). Ring is a HAND SKETCH around the Vatican Hill (+-150 m); tower spacing = sketched perimeter / 44; width 3 m is a guess.

fires.name: Great Fire of Rome
fires.note: Began 18-19 July 64 in the shops around the Circus Maximus, between the Caelian and Palatine (S24); burned 6 + 3 days; 10 of 14 districts. Ring is a small hand sketch around the Circus area, not the burned area; no building destroyed.

title: ROME
753 BC TO NOW

cards.title: Rome begins on the Palatine
lines: Tradition dates the first settlements around the Palatine Hill to 753 BC.

cards.title: No more kings
lines: The last king, Tarquin the Proud, is expelled.
Rome becomes a republic.

cards.title: The Gauls sack Rome
lines: After the Battle of the Allia the Gauls burn the city.
Defenders hold the Capitoline Hill.

cards.title: Circus Maximus
lines: Permanent wooden starting stalls are built in 329 BC.
Later it spans 621 by 118 meters, the largest stadium in ancient Rome.

cards.title: The first road and aqueduct
lines: The Appian Way and the Aqua Appia are both begun in 312 BC.

cards.title: Carthage destroyed
lines: After six days of assault the Romans destroy their rival.

cards.title: The Ides of March
lines: Julius Caesar is assassinated by a group of senators.

cards.title: Augustus, first emperor
lines: The Republic ends and the Empire begins.
He is said to have found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble.

cards.title: Theatre of Marcellus
lines: Completed in 13 BC and formally inaugurated in 12 BC by Augustus.

cards.title: The Great Fire
lines: Nearly three quarters of Rome is destroyed: 10 of its 14 districts.

cards.title: The Colosseum opens
lines: Begun under Vespasian in 72, completed under Titus in 80.

cards.title: Trajan's Column
lines: Dedicated in 113, about 35 meters tall with its pedestal.

cards.title: The Pantheon
lines: Rebuilt under Hadrian and probably dedicated around 126.

cards.title: Hadrian's Mausoleum
lines: Erected on the right bank of the Tiber between 134 and 139.
Today it is known as Castel Sant'Angelo.

cards.title: A city of a million or more
lines: Estimates of Rome's peak population range from 450,000 to over 3.5 million.
Historians favor 1 to 2 million.

cards.title: Baths of Caracalla
lines: Inaugurated in 216, they are among the great imperial baths.

cards.title: A wall for the whole city
lines: The Aurelian Walls run 19 km around 13.7 square km.

cards.title: The largest baths of all
lines: Built from 298 to 306 under Diocletian.

cards.title: Maxentius's basilica
lines: Begun by Maxentius in 308, finished by Constantine in 312.

cards.title: Old St. Peter's
lines: Constantine orders a basilica over the site of the Circus of Nero.

cards.title: Alaric sacks Rome
lines: The Visigoths enter through the Salarian Gate and pillage the city for three days.

cards.title: The Vandals sack Rome
lines: A second sack, more destructive than the first.

cards.title: The Western Empire ends
lines: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, the last emperor in the West.

cards.title: Byzantine Rome
lines: General Belisarius recaptures the city for the Eastern Empire on 9 December.

cards.title: Totila enters Rome
lines: His Goths scale the walls at night and open the Porta Asinaria.

cards.title: A city of 30,000
lines: After the Gothic War the population may have fallen to about 30,000.

cards.title: Plague, and an angel
lines: Legend says the Archangel Michael sheathed his sword above the tomb of Hadrian.
It marks the end of the plague.

cards.title: The Papal State
lines: The pope becomes a sovereign ruler. The Papal States last until 1870.

cards.title: Charlemagne
lines: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor, in Old St. Peter's.

cards.title: The Leonine Wall
lines: A three-kilometer wall encircles the Vatican Hill for the first time.

cards.title: The Normans
lines: Italo-Normans sack Rome, called in by Pope Gregory VII.

cards.title: The popes leave
lines: Clement V moves the papal court to Avignon for 67 years.

cards.title: The popes return
lines: Gregory XI reinstates the Holy See in Rome.
The city has fewer than 20,000 people.

cards.title: A new St. Peter's
lines: Construction of the present basilica begins on 18 April.

cards.title: The Sack of Rome
lines: Mutinous troops of Charles V capture the city.
The pope takes refuge in Castel Sant'Angelo.

cards.title: Bernini's square
lines: The colonnades of St. Peter's Square are finished.

cards.title: Trevi Fountain
lines: Work began in 1732. Giuseppe Pannini completes it in 1762.

cards.title: A Roman Republic
lines: French troops occupy Rome and a sister republic is proclaimed.

cards.title: Napoleon annexes Rome
lines: Rome becomes part of the First French Empire until 1814.

cards.title: Another Roman Republic
lines: Led by Mazzini, it ends when the French Army enters on 3 July and restores the Pope.

cards.title: Italy is united
lines: The Kingdom of Italy forms with Florence as its temporary capital.

cards.title: Capital of Italy
lines: Italian troops breach the wall near Porta Pia on 20 September 1870.
Rome becomes the capital on 3 February 1871.

cards.title: A growing capital
lines: The census counts 273,952 residents.

cards.title: March on Rome
lines: Blackshirts approach the capital, and Mussolini comes to power.

cards.title: Vatican City
lines: The Lateran Pacts recognize Vatican City as an independent state.

cards.title: EUR
lines: Mussolini plans a new district for the 1942 World's Fair.

cards.title: Liberation
lines: American and British troops liberate Rome on June 3-4.

cards.title: A republic
lines: Rome becomes the capital of the Italian Republic.

cards.title: Termini Station
lines: The new station is inaugurated.

cards.title: A city of 1.65 million
lines: The census counts 1,651,754 residents.

cards.title: Peak population
lines: The census counts 2,781,993 residents, the highest on record.
